text:
support-bot: Escalation from ACME (INC-412) — customer reports builds breaking after upgrading our Go SDK to a v2 tagged release. They say it worked before, now CI errors. Logs + repro below.

alex: Thanks — can you paste the minimal go.mod and the exact go build output?

sam: Pasting what customer sent (sanitized):
```
module github.com/acme/service

go 1.20

require (
    github.com/redwood/sdk v2.0.1 // indirect
)

// error from CI:
# golang.org/x/mod/module
../../pkg/mod/cache/download/github.com/redwood/sdk/@v/v2.0.1.zip: malformed module path
build command-line-arguments
../../pkg/mod/cache/download/github.com/redwood/sdk/@v/v2.0.1.zip: unrecognized import path "github.com/redwood/sdk/v2": missing dot in first path element
```

morgan: Two things jumping out: 1) module path vs tag mismatch (v2 requires module path to include /v2), 2) they also see GOPROXY fetch issues sometimes with private mirrors. Are they using our hosted proxy or a private proxy?

sam: Customer uses org proxy + GitHub Packages for private modules. CI log also had a 401 when trying to fetch the module: 
```
GET https://proxy.company.com/github.com/redwood/sdk/@v/v2.0.1.info 401 Unauthorized
```

alex: Ok. Common pattern: if the module was tagged v2 but the module stanza inside the SDK's go.mod didn't include "/v2", `go` will complain. Another angle: CI may be hitting a GOPROXY that doesn't support auth or returns 401. Two separate failures could be happening.

morgan: Quick repro I ran locally (inside golang:1.20 image):
```bash
# reproduce
mkdir repro && cd repro
go mod init temp/repro
cat > main.go <<'EOF'
package main
import _ "github.com/redwood/sdk/v2"
func main() {}
EOF
# try to build
go build ./...
```
Result: "module declares its path: github.com/redwood/sdk, but was required as github.com/redwood/sdk/v2"

sam: Customer had a `replace` in their go.mod pointing to `github.com/redwood/sdk => github.com/redwood/sdk v1.9.0` (they were trying to force old) which made things worse when the tagged v2 was fetched by transitive deps.

alex: Two remediation paths: (A) fix the upstream SDK repo to include the correct module path (`module github.com/redwood/sdk/v2`) and ensure tagged v2 releases are semver + module-path consistent, OR (B) pin imports to the non-v2 import path (use v1) across the codebase. For CI GOPROXY 401, set GOPRIVATE or configure auth token in CI.

morgan: For CI we suggested these commands to customer:
```bash
# set GOPRIVATE so go bypasses proxy for private modules
go env -w GOPRIVATE=github.com/acme,github.com/redwood
# or configure authenticated proxy access via env (example for GitHub):
export GOPRIVATE=github.com/acme
export GOPROXY=https://proxy.company.com,direct
export GOPROXY_USER=... # configure token in CI secret manager
```

ci-bot: Confirmed: when GOPRIVATE set, the 401 disappears but then another error appears when fetching v2: "module declares its path \"github.com/redwood/sdk\"; new import path requires /v2".

sam: So root cause is the SDK repo release process: tag v2 but didn't update module path. Workaround for customer: add a temporary local replace to point at a fork that has corrected go.mod, e.g.:
```
replace github.com/redwood/sdk/v2 => github.com/acme/forked-sdk/v2 v2.0.1-fix
```
But that isn't great for long-term or for CI reproducibility unless you host the fork in reachable proxy.

alex: Can engineering (eng-ml/eng-runtime) confirm if our v2 tag release pipeline missed updating module path? @morgan can you file an internal issue? I'll also escalate to the SDK owner.

morgan: Filed REDWOOD-ISSUE-2377 with logs + reproduction steps. Assigned to @jamie (SDK owner). Suggest adding a release validation check: after tagging, run `go list -m all` and ensure module path matches tag or run `go mod tidy` and quick build.

sam: Customer accepted a temporary mitigation: configure GOPRIVATE in CI and add replace -> internal fork. They're blocked for release but ok with a short-term patch.

alex: Next steps: 1) eng to patch SDK repo and cut a compatible v2 tag with correct `module` line; 2) docs: add guidance on v2 module path rules and CI GOPRIVATE auth setup; 3) notify customer once patched. I'll follow up in INC-412.

support-bot: Marking this thread as triaged. /cc INC-412 link: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INC-412 :white_check_mark:
